transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-13 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Ramos, Priya Nambiar (Redwood); Liam O'Connor, Nadia Patel, Samir Qureshi, Jenna Park (Cobalt)

Summary (auto): quick sync on pilot acceleration, validate latency SLO at p99, confirm Dedicated commit thresholds, agree next steps for bench runs and security docs.

00:00 - Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate you carving time in the sprint, quick roll call?
00:06 - Liam O'Connor: yep hi, Liam here, we got the core infra folks and product, thanks Maya
00:10 - Maya Chen: awesome, Diego from our infra team is on for the perf deep dive, and Priya is here for handoffs
00:18 - Diego Ramos: hey all, quick note, today's goal is to align pilot acceptance criteria and lay out bench plan, not a sales pitch, promise
00:26 - Nadia Patel: sounds good, we have some uptime questions and our finance team wants clear cost delta for Dedicated, also security has some VPC questions
00:35 - Maya Chen: perfect, we'll tackle those in order. Liam can you sketch current traffic? top endpoints, request size distribution, any burstiness?
00:43 - Liam O'Connor: yeah so product calls an assistant endpoint, median prompt tokens ~120, outputs ~200, but we have spikes during batch analytics runs where concurrency can jump 6x for 10-15 minutes, that's the main worry
00:58 - Jenna Park: and those bursts correlate with nightly jobs which we can't shift easily, so tail latency matters more than average for UX
01:07 - Diego Ramos: thanks, that's helpful — for those patterns we typically recommend Dedicated with burst policies or hybrid routing; auto-burst can spill to hosted fallback if capacity is exhausted
01:18 - Samir Qureshi: hmm, can you explain the fallback? our security team is wary of data crossing tenancy boundaries even in fallback cases
01:26 - Diego Ramos: yes, good point — fallback can be to a model variant that doesn't persist customer KV, and we can enable strict data controls; but true no-cross-tenancy fallback requires routing to your private deployment or pre-provisioned warm nodes
01:39 - Nadia Patel: how does that affect cost? our finance asks — is Dedicated a big uplift vs hosted? we want numbers and a run rate model
01:48 - Maya Chen: short answer: Dedicated raises base commit costs but lowers per-token unit economics during normal ops; we'll send a modeled delta showing committed vs on-demand run-rates with examples at your concurrency profile
02:00 - Liam O'Connor: ok send that, and also we need p99 latency numbers, we saw in the trial p99 was 1.2s but sometimes spiked to 3.8s and that broke an internal SLA
02:13 - Diego Ramos: those spikes could be kernel warmup or unusual sequence length outliers; Diego: we'll instrument KV/cache hit rates, batching behavior, and quantify tail causes — suggest a bench that mimics your burst window and long-seq cases
02:26 - Samir Qureshi: network will matter too — our VPC peering has 7ms baseline, but queueing on our side during spikes is likely; can Redwood run bench both over our peering and via hosted path?
02:37 - Priya Nambiar: yes we can do both, Diego will propose scripts; Diego: also we have quantization recommendations for cost; could that change p99?
02:47 - Diego Ramos: quantization normally reduces latency slightly on GPU bound paths, but for small sequences effects are mixed; more important is batching and prefix caching. if your workload reuses prompts we can show big wins with prefix caching
03:00 - Nadia Patel: prompt reuse is high for our classification flows, less so for freeform generation — we'll label sets accordingly when we send prompts
03:09 - Jenna Park: security — SOC2 and SSO were fine in the docs you sent but two items remain: audit log retention to 7 years and HSM integration for key wrapping
03:21 - Maya Chen: noted; Redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations and long-retention audit logs as an add-on; I'll attach the implementation note. For pilot, we can provide temporary extended logs for the trial period
03:34 - Samir Qureshi: any constraints on on-prem or air-gapped? we might explore private later for regulated customers
03:41 - Diego Ramos: our Private deployment supports on-prem and air-gapped installs; pilot can start hosted/dedicated while we scope Private if needed; that'll be a separate procurement track
03:51 - Liam O'Connor: procurement will want a rough timeline and cost bucket for private — can you give a ballpark?
03:57 - Maya Chen: ballpark yes: Private tends to be a multi-month engagement with a platform license plus optional support tiers; we'll include a note but it's not final until we scope network and infra footprint
04:09 - Nadja (sic) speaker mislabel: the transcript tool mis-typed Nadja; Nadia clarifies: we also need RBAC ties to our SSO groups so ops access aligns with our roles
04:20 - Diego Ramos: we support SCIM and SAML provisioning, RBAC mapping, and per-route keys; we'll include an RBAC mapping template for your ops roles
04:30 - Maya Chen: ok to recap — Diego will run bench scripts that mimic burst and long sequences (week of 3/23), Samir to share network topology, Nadia to share prompt sets, and Maya to send pricing and security addendum. Anything else?
04:45 - Jenna Park: finance will want a 12-month run-rate with both optimistic and conservative adoption scenarios, can you model both?
04:52 - Maya Chen: yes we'll include conservative/optimistic for commit sizing and also an example showing cost if you use batching & prefix caching vs naive calls
05:02 - Liam O'Connor: timeline to sign? product needs commitment by end of April to include in Q2 roadmap
05:09 - Maya Chen: that's doable if pilot completes in April and results meet p99 SLOs; our target is to have bench + pilot readout by 2026-04-20
05:19 - Samir Qureshi: can Redwood provide an SLA addendum for Dedicated? latency SLOs particularly for p99 during normal ops
05:27 - Priya Nambiar: Dedicated comes with SLA options, we can draft an addendum; typical is uptime SLA plus latency targets tied to config; we'll propose a templated SLA you can review
05:38 - Nadia Patel: great, last item — any competitor differences we should be aware of from your perspective?
05:43 - Diego Ramos: competitors like OpenAI have good throughput but less built-for-enterprise dedicated routing and private deploy options; Anthropic is strong on safety models; VendorX is cheaper but lacks our batching/cache controls — we'll include a short note in the follow-up
05:56 - Maya Chen: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow-up with materials and schedule the bench kickoff. Priya will help coordinate slots.
06:05 - Liam O'Connor: thanks all, appreciate the clarity

End transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels, some filler words and truncated sentences; technical terms may be slightly garbled (e.g., KV cache shown as K-V cache, private deploy spelled Private Deploy/Priv-Deploy in places).
